key_insight: AI analysis identified three cerebellar imaging subtypes of schizophrenia with distinct inferred patterns of gray matter loss and biological characteristics.
clinical_relevance: Subtype-associated differences in symptoms and treatment response may inform future stratification research but are not validated for guiding individual care.
method: Applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) to cross-sectional 3D cerebellar MRI.
Identified trajectories originating in lobules X, III and VIIb.
Examined subtype associations with connectivity, gene expression, symptoms and treatment response.
evidence_signal: The study included 3,550 patients and 5,771 controls across 34 sites, replicated subtype trajectories in two independent patient samples, and examined treatment data from 381 patients followed for up to 12 months.
watch_item: Trajectories were inferred from cross-sectional MRI rather than observed longitudinal progression; prospective validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: Three Cerebellar Imaging Subtypes in Schizophrenia with Distinct Spatiotemporal Trajectories and Biological Characteristics
